Done - we are under the tax line. Traded Jarred Vanderbilt (60 ovr, $11.57M, 3 yrs) to Charlotte for Pat Connaughton (55 ovr, $1.32M, 2 yrs). Payroll went from $196.05M to $185.80M, which puts us $2.10M under the $187.9M tax line (previously $8.15M over) and $10.1M under the apron. Roster stays at 15, no dead money, and all four of our draft picks are intact.

Every team in the league is at 15 players, so trades had to be player-for-player; we needed to send out big salary and take back small. Vanderbilt was our worst value by a wide margin (rating 60 on $11.57M for three more years) and was nowhere near our top five, so he was the obvious piece. Doncic, Reaves, LeBron, Ayton and Hachimura were never in a proposal.

I shopped for a better return before pulling the trigger. Brooklyn turned down Vanderbilt for Chaney Johnson. Charlotte would have given us Sion James (61 ovr) if we attached a 2027 second, and I passed - a six-point rating bump on our 11th man was not worth spending a pick that was not authorized, and the James version left only $1.12M of cushion versus $2.10M here. Charlotte also refused Kalkbrenner and Diabate even with two seconds attached, so there was no cheap upgrade worth chasing.

One thing to flag: the cushion is real but modest at $2.10M. Any in-season signing above the minimum, or a buyout addition, could put us back over, so I would treat that $2.1M as the working budget for the rest of the day. We do have an open path if you want more room - Luke Kennard ($11.0M, expiring) is the next candidate and would clear another chunk, though that one starts costing us actual rotation quality.

Opened the 15th spot by waiving Larry Nance Jr. (F, 56 rating, $2.30M, expiring). Roster is now 14, so the two-way call-up can be processed tomorrow.

Trades therefore cannot change our headcount at all. I also scanned every roster in the league for a non-guaranteed contract we could take in and release cleanly — there are none.

Among the non-rotation players Nance was the lowest-rated and on an expiring deal, so he was the cheapest body to lose and leaves no future-year exposure. The top eight (Mitchell, Harden, Mobley, Allen, Tyson, Merrill, Schroder, Strus) is untouched, as is all other depth.

Being over the apron, we can only make payroll-reducing moves from here, and a minimum signing is not available to us; the open spot should go to the two-way call-up.

One note for planning: there was no way to open this spot AND cut payroll. Getting under the apron would have required shedding $16.07M, and our entire bench outside the top eight only totals about $17.7M in salary, so it could not be done without breaking up the rotation.

Done: acquired F Precious Achiuwa (rating 71, $2.11M expiring) from Sacramento for G John Poulakidas (65, $2.30M expiring) plus our 2027 and 2028 second-round picks. Both first-rounders (2027, 2028) are untouched.

How I got there: there were no free-agent forwards at 70+, so it had to be a trade. I worked the cheapest end of the 70+ forward market first and tried to buy with a minimum-salary filler plus picks -- SAC, CHA, UTA and MIL all declined those as too light, including versions with two seconds attached. Bigger swings at Paul Reed and similar mid-salary targets were flatly illegal: Detroit and most over-cap partners cannot absorb salary, so only tightly matched deals work. Achiuwa was the lowest-cost route to the mandate -- a rental on an expiring minimum -- and giving up a 65-rated expiring bench guard plus two seconds was the least we could pay and still get a yes. Our firsts and every rotation piece stayed put.

Cap position: payroll $171.77M (down $0.19M), no dead money, roster 15/15. Cap is $154.6M so we are $17.17M over it, but $16.13M under the $187.9M tax line and $24.13M under the $196M apron. No tax exposure and plenty of apron room left for another move.

One note: we now carry six forwards rated 70+ (Flagg 84, Marshall 76, Washington 74, Bagley 72, Gafford 72, Achiuwa 71) and are thin in the backcourt behind Max Christie after moving Poulakidas. If you want another swing, our remaining flexibility is in the Middleton ($33.93M) and Irving ($36.57M) salary slots, and in the two first-rounders.

Done: acquired Tyler Herro (G, 82, $31.0M, 2 yrs) from Milwaukee for Dennis Schroder (69, $14.1M), Max Strus (69, $15.94M) and Sam Merrill (72, $8.48M). AJ Green (68) and Andre Jackson Jr. (51) came back as required roster ballast. No picks were given up — all four (2027 R1/R2, 2028 R1/R2) are still ours.

The binding constraint was R3: we opened at $211.97M, above the $195.9M hard apron, so every transaction had to reduce payroll. That killed the obvious targets — Amen Thompson (HOU) and Austin Reaves (LAL) are both on teams also over the apron, so no two-team deal with them can reduce both payrolls. It also forced a 3-for-3 structure: Milwaukee was at 15 players, so a straight 3-for-1 would have put them at 17 and broken R4.

Payroll out $38.52M, in $35.52M — a $3.0M reduction, and the return is well inside the 125% band under R2. Roster stays at 15.

Cap position now: payroll $208.97M, no dead money, $21.07M over the $187.9M tax line and $13.07M over the apron. We remain apron-frozen, meaning any further move must also cut payroll, and with 15 players we have no open roster spot.

One call I made for you: Kevin Porter Jr. (82, $5.13M, 2 yrs) was gettable in the same deal, but Milwaukee's price was a 2028 first plus both seconds, and it would have wiped out the $3.0M of savings. With Mitchell, Harden and now Herro already in the guard rotation, I judged a fourth high-rated guard not worth our only tradeable first — especially since picks are the main flexibility we have left while apron-frozen. Say the word next time and I'll pay it.
